consensus_summary: The remnant is the small faithful minority of God’s people whom He graciously preserves through judgment, exile, or apostasy, securing covenant continuity; it functions as both a sign of severe judgment and of hope, and is applied by Paul to the elect remnant chosen by grace.
book_summary: The faithful few preserved and gathered from what remains, illustrated by gleanings left at the field’s edge and gold separated from dross.
consensus_core_identification: faithful minority preserved by divine grace through judgment
book_core_identification: faithful few preserved and gathered from what remains
rationale: Both identify the remnant as the faithful few whom God preserves out of a larger whole that undergoes loss or judgment. The book’s added similes (gleanings; refined gold) are drawn directly from the same scriptural cluster already central to the consensus (Ruth 2; Zech 13; 1 Kgs 19; Rom 11) and do not alter referent, conditions, or covered cases; differences are purely illustrative wording.
strongest_objection: The explicit agricultural and metallurgical imagery might be read as narrowing the remnant to a specifically ‘leftover/purified’ subset, yet the consensus already includes precisely those texts and the same dual sense of survival-plus-refinement.
